pr_body:
…rt implementation for their platform

Motivation:

At the moment most users manually check if netty provides a native implementation for their platform and if so select it. This pattern is present in almost all code bases by end-users. We should provide this functionality out of the box so users dont need to maintain it by themselves.

Modifications:

Add TransportSelector which will pick the right Channel / EventLoopGroup implementation based on the platform and what native libs are on the classpath

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10076

review_comment:
this is a bit of a nit (in response to the above):
Why not just create a small class to hold all of them.

```java
TransportSelections selections = TransportSelector.selectOptionalForNative();
```

Something like `TransportSelections`, `TransportStrategy`, `TransportSettings`, `TransportConfiguration`, etc. might make sense. It might also lend itself to being more DI-friendly.

However, rather than `Tuple#configureBootstrap(Bootstrap)`, I think the opposite direction would be more user-friendly, something like `Bootstrap#configure(Tuple)`.

I think tuple is a bit of an anti-pattern on the GC side of things and it's not commonly used by netty, unless it's some kind of `static final` variables.
But since it's only used one time during app bootstrap it doesn't matter much...

As I mentioned in the other issue, there are some use cases where users or applications may prefer to fail outright, rather than silently defaulting to a non-native transport. E.g., perhaps you expect Epoll to be available, and silently defaulting to Nio might have dangerous performance implications.

I'm okay with saying that is too niche of a use case for us to be concerned with here, but I'm also wondering if we should we consider offering some way to *require* a native transport? Perhaps an accompanying `NativeTransportSelector`? Or `require` variations of the methods?
